question.text: A trader buys 10 bond futures contracts at Rs. 101.20 and sells them at Rs. 102.00. Face value is Rs. 2,00,000 per contract. Brokerage is 0.01% of contract value on each leg. What is the net profit after brokerage?

explanation.text: The Logic: Gross profit per contract = (102.00 - 101.20)/100 x 2,00,000 = 0.80/100 x 2,00,000 = Rs. 1,600. Total gross = 1,600 x 10 = Rs. 16,000. Buy side contract value = 10 x 2,00,000 x 101.20/100 = Rs. 20,24,000. Sell side contract value = 10 x 2,00,000 x 102.00/100 = Rs. 20,40,000. Buy brokerage = 20,24,000 x 0.0001 = Rs. 202.40. Sell brokerage = 20,40,000 x 0.0001 = Rs. 204.00. Total brokerage = Rs. 406.40. Net profit = 16,000 - 406.40 = Rs. 15,593.60. The Trap: Rs. 16,000 ignores brokerage. Rs. 15,600 uses flat Rs. 400 brokerage. Rs. 14,000 double-counts brokerage. Note: GOI bond futures contract value is computed on face value and price, and futures brokerage is charged on contract value for both legs. Apply brokerage to the buy and sell side separately.
